final_message:
Fixed. The reproducing test now passes, along with the rest of the suite (25 passed).

The bug was in `collect` in `billing/payments.py`. When the gateway charge failed, the `else` branch was just `pass`, so `record_failure` was never called. The failed payment never moved the subscription to `past_due` and never scheduled a retry. I replaced the `pass` with `record_failure(ctx, invoice, result["failure_code"])`.

I added your test as `tests/test_recovery.py`, and `answer.json` in the repo root says `payments.py` / `collect`.

steps.command: cd billing && ls && wc -l *.py && grep -n "past_due\|def advance\|retry" *.py ../tests/conftest.py | head -60
cd billing && cat dunning.py engine.py; sed -n 1,50p ../tests/conftest.py

cd .. && python3 - <<'E'
p='billing/payments.py'
s=open(p).read().replace("    else:\n        pass\n","    else:\n        record_failure(ctx, invoice, result[\"failure_code\"])\n")
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
echo '{"file": "payments.py", "function": "collect"}' > answer.json
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5

cat >> tests/test_recovery.py <<'E'


def test_recovery_after_retry_succeeds(world):
    cus = world.customer()
    world.gateway.fail_next.append("card_declined")
    sub = world.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(world.monthly["id"], 1)])
    assert sub["status"] == "past_due"
    world.advance_days(1)
    assert sub["status"] == "active"
    [inv] = world.engine.invoices_for(cus["id"])
    assert inv["status"] == "paid"
E
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -3
